samples.summary: Detected link spans accept URL userinfo, so a painted span can read as one host and navigate to another — now reachable by a plain click from read-only viewers
samples.evidence: `URL_CHAR` (cell-links.ts:36) includes `@`, and `toUrl` (cell-links.ts:149-157) gates only on `isSafeUrl`, which checks `new URL(href).protocol` and nothing about the authority. So the cell text `https://accounts.example.com@evil.test/login` is detected as one span, painted underlined in link colour exactly as written, and recorded as `RenderedLink.url` verbatim. `worksheet.ts:3688` then does `window.open(link.url, '_blank', …)` — and because of the new read-only branch at `worksheet.ts:3681` (`this.readOnly || e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey`), a share-link viewer reaches `evil.test` with an ordinary left click, no modifier and no confirmation. Attack: any collaborator (or the person who shares the doc) writes such a string into a cell; every viewer who clicks the visibly-trusted prefix is navigated to the attacker host. Two things widen this beyond the deleted `url-detect.ts`: detection moved from "the whole cell value is a URL" to "any substring", so the spoof can hide inside prose in any cell, and the plain-click path is new. The hover card's `toLabel` (SheetLinkPopover.tsx:20-32) shows the true `parsed.host`, but it only appears after the 300 ms `LinkHoverDelayMS` (worksheet.ts:138) — a click that beats that delay never sees it, and `handleMouseDown` does not consult it. `docs/tasks/active/20260917-sheets-cell-link-spans-todo.md` lists this under "Known limitations" ("Userinfo still reads as the host … the underline and the modifier-click are not [honest]"), so it is acknowledged but shipped unmitigated; no test in `packages/sheets/src/view/__tests__/cell-links.test.ts` covers a userinfo authority. A cheap fix is to refuse a span whose parsed `URL` has non-empty `username`/`password`, or to strip userinfo before recording the destination.

samples.summary: `trimTrailing` is O(L²) per span and runs inside the paint loop, giving an attacker-controlled cell a per-frame cost blow-up the new linearity tests cannot detect
samples.evidence: `trimTrailing` (cell-links.ts:118-143) removes one trailing character per outer iteration, and for every closing bracket it re-slices and re-splits the *entire* remaining span: `const span = text.slice(0, end); span.split(pair[0]); span.split(pair[1])` (lines 131-133). That is O(L) work per removed character, i.e. O(L²) per span, with L bounded only by `MaxUrlLength = 2048`. The forward-walk bound does not help: a cell value of `('https://' + ')'.repeat(2000) + ' ')` repeated stops the URL-char walk at each space, so `overlong` (line 276-277) is false and the full 2008-char span is handed to `trimTrailing`, which then performs ~2000 iterations × two `split()` calls over a ~2000-char string, each allocating a ~2000-element array — roughly 12M char operations and 4M array slots per 2 kB of cell text. `gridcanvas.ts` calls `detectLinks` per line, per visible cell, per frame (`const linkSpans = lines.map((line) => detectLinks(line))`), so a 32 kB cell costs ~16 such blocks every frame. That is the same availability failure §6 of the design doc says the scanner exists to prevent — a collaborator (or a CSV/import) planting one cell freezes the grid for everyone who has it on screen, read-only share-link viewers included. The suite cannot catch it: `cell-links.test.ts:168-186` asserts only the *growth ratio* at n vs 4n, and this defect is linear in n with a ~6000× constant, so the ratio stays near 4 and the test passes. None of the five adversarial fixtures contains a closing bracket. Fix: count brackets once with an incremental scan instead of re-splitting per iteration.

samples.summary: Read-only plain-click turns every painted span into one-click navigation to a destination controlled by whoever can write the document
samples.evidence: `(this.readOnly || e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey)` at worksheet.ts:3681 removes the modifier requirement for viewers, so in a view-only share link an ordinary left click anywhere inside a recorded link box calls `window.open(link.url, '_blank', 'noopener,noreferrer')` (worksheet.ts:3688) before any selection handling. Combined with the fact that detection now fires on substrings of any cell (including formula results, since the `cell?.f` guard was dropped in gridcanvas.ts), a single editor can make large parts of a viewed sheet navigate on the click a viewer would otherwise use to select a cell — to `http://localhost:…` service endpoints, to a credential-harvesting page, or to the userinfo-spoofed host described in the other finding. `noopener,noreferrer` is correctly applied so there is no opener/referrer leak; the residual risk is unconsented navigation to an author-chosen destination with no visible URL beforehand. Consider requiring the hover card (or a hostname-bearing affordance) to have been shown before the plain-click path fires, or keeping the modifier for cross-origin destinations.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the working tree. `URL_CHAR` at packages/sheets/src/view/cell-links.ts:36 includes `@`, so the forward scan at cell-links.ts:270-287 swallows a userinfo authority into a single span and records `url` verbatim. The only gate is `toUrl` (cell-links.ts:149-157) -> `isSafeUrl` (packages/core/src/url/index.ts:58-65), which inspects only `new URL(href).protocol` against SAFE_PROTOCOLS and says nothing about username/password/host; a repo-wide grep finds no userinfo handling anywhere in packages/sheets or packages/core. The destination is then navigated to without confirmation at packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:3688 (`window.open(link.url, '_blank', 'noopener,noreferrer')`) under the branch at worksheet.ts:3678-3682, whose `this.readOnly || e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey` condition means a read-only share-link viewer opens it with a plain left click. The only place the true host is shown is the hover card's `toLabel` (SheetLinkPopover.tsx:20-32), which is gated behind `LinkHoverDelayMS = 300` (worksheet.ts:139, timer at worksheet.ts:996) and is never consulted by `handleMouseDown`, so it does not make the click path unreachable or safe; the popover's own filter (SheetLinkPopover.tsx:58) is the same `isSafeUrl`. No test in packages/sheets/src/view/__tests__/cell-links.test.ts covers a userinfo authority, and docs/tasks/active/20260917-sheets-cell-link-spans-todo.md:232-235 explicitly ships it as a known limitation ("Userinfo still reads as the host… the underline and the modifier-click are not [honest]"). This is unsafe handling of untrusted document content producing a spoofed navigation destination — in the security lane, and not refutable on any named ground.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repository. `trimTrailing` (cell-links.ts:118-143) decrements `end` by one per iteration and, for every closing bracket, re-runs `text.slice(0,end)` plus two `split()` calls over the whole remaining span (lines 131-133) — O(L) work per removed character, i.e. O(L^2) per span. The path is reachable: `')'` is in URL_CHAR (line 36), so a cell value of `('https://' + ')'.repeat(2000) + ' ')` repeated yields a 2008-char run that stops short of `limit` (line 270), making `overlong` false (lines 276-277) and handing the full span to `trimTrailing` at line 278 — ~2000 iterations x two splits over a ~2000-char string, per 2008-char block. After trimming, `span.length > scheme.length` fails (line 283) so nothing is emitted, and `schemeAt`'s first-character gate (lines 167-170) prevents re-entry inside the paren run, so cost is linear in block count with a ~6000x constant. That is exactly why the growth-ratio assertion at cell-links.test.ts:181-189 passes, and none of the five fixtures (lines 170-180) contains a closing bracket ('https://[' uses an opening one). gridcanvas.ts:1696 calls detectLinks per line, per visible cell, inside renderCellContent on a full every-frame repaint, so a planted cell degrades the grid for every viewer including read-only ones — the precise availability failure docs/design/sheets/sheet-hyperlink.md:209-243 says the scanner exists to prevent, and a third super-linear path that neither documented bound (MaxEmailLocal, MaxUrlLength) covers. The other caller (emailAt, line 234) passes bracket-free EMAIL_DOMAIN_CHAR text and so is not a guard for this site. I found no cell-value length cap in packages/sheets. Attacker-controlled algorithmic-complexity DoS on untrusted document content (CWE-1333/CWE-400) is unsafe input handling in my lane, not a general logic bug; no named refutation ground applies.
